item.text: I’m building the 2B record around the actual Nigeria-ECOWAS/Niger episode, since that is the only clear international-peace exposure in 2023. I’m opening the ECOWAS, UN, congressional, and reporting sources that can separate diplomacy from coercion and show what Tinubu could and could not do.

item.text:
**Overview**

Nigeria did not enter 2023 in an interstate war, and Tinubu did not launch a war of choice in 2023. The main international-peace exposure was the Niger coup crisis, where Tinubu’s government, acting through ECOWAS chairmanship, combined sanctions pressure with repeated diplomacy and a threatened standby force. The record shows restraint under real pressure: force was discussed, but the public, documented path in 2023 kept returning to dialogue, regional coordination, and restoration of constitutional order. ([ecowas.int](https://www.ecowas.int/ecowas-heads-of-state-to-hold-extraordinary-summit-on-the-political-situation-in-the-republic-of-niger/), [statehouse.gov.ng](https://statehouse.gov.ng/niger-republic-at-2nd-ecowas-extraordinary-summit-president-tinubu-champions-dialogue-to-resolve-impasse/))

Tinubu’s authority here was partly direct and partly constrained. He could chair ECOWAS and set Nigeria’s diplomatic posture, but any use of force depended on a regional bloc with internal disagreement, on Nigeria’s army already being tied down domestically, and on other states pushing for diplomacy. The strongest 2023 evidence therefore supports a chapter about coercive crisis management with significant restraint, not about war initiation. ([amp.dw.com](https://amp.dw.com/en/niger-how-might-an-ecowas-military-intervention-unfold/a-66431072), [amp.dw.com](https://amp.dw.com/en/nigeria-senate-cautions-against-niger-military-intervention/a-66450388))

**Evidence Index**

1. **ECOWAS framed Niger as a constitutional-order crisis, not a war of conquest**
- **Claim:** On July 28, 2023, ECOWAS announced that Tinubu, as chair of the Authority of Heads of State and Government, had convened an emergency summit on Niger’s political situation. This matters because it shows the crisis was handled through a regional constitutional-order process, not unilateral Nigerian military action.
- **Best source:** ECOWAS, “ECOWAS Heads of State to hold Extraordinary Summit on the Political Situation in the Republic of Niger,” July 28, 2023. Direct link: [ecowas.int](https://www.ecowas.int/ecowas-heads-of-state-to-hold-extraordinary-summit-on-the-political-situation-in-the-republic-of-niger/)
- **Locator:** Lines 68-71 say Tinubu convened the summit and that the leaders would discuss Niger’s political situation and recent developments. ([ecowas.int](https://www.ecowas.int/ecowas-heads-of-state-to-hold-extraordinary-summit-on-the-political-situation-in-the-republic-of-niger/))
- **Period type:** Target-period contemporaneous.
- **Ruler attribution:** Direct. Tinubu was the convening chair.
- **Complicating evidence:** ECOWAS was divided, and later reporting shows several members resisted force.
- **Caution:** This is a summit notice, not the summit outcome.
- **Independent support:** Reuters coverage of the same deadline-and-sanctions episode; DW’s summary of the military option. ([reuters.com via ThePrint/Investing](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/west-african-leaders-meet-over-niger-coup-junta-warns-against-intervention-3138325), [dw.com](https://amp.dw.com/en/niger-how-might-an-ecowas-military-intervention-unfold/a-66431072))

2. **ECOWAS did threaten force and impose sanctions, but still preserved a diplomatic track**
- **Claim:** ECOWAS’s August 10, 2023 communique shows that the bloc kept sanctions and force on the table while still grounding its approach in diplomacy and dialogue. This matters because it is the clearest evidence that Tinubu’s regional posture was coercive but not reckless: the bloc sought leverage without immediately escalating to war.
- **Best source:** ECOWAS, “Final Communique – Second Extraordinary Summit...,” August 10, 2023. Direct link: [ecowas.int](https://www.ecowas.int/final-communique-second-extraordinary-summit-of-the-ecowas-authority-of-heads-of-state-and-government-on-the-political-situation-in-niger/)
- **Locator:** The page identifies the final communique and its accompanying PDF. Search-result text for the same communiqué and Reuters summaries report sanctions, a standby force, and continued diplomacy. ([ecowas.int](https://www.ecowas.int/final-communique-second-extraordinary-summit-of-the-ecowas-authority-of-heads-of-state-and-government-on-the-political-situation-in-niger/), [theprint.in](https://theprint.in/world/west-african-leaders-meet-over-niger-coup-junta-warns-against-intervention/1692097/))
- **Period type:** Target-period contemporaneous.
- **Ruler attribution:** Strong but indirect. Tinubu chaired the summit, but the decision was regional.
- **Complicating evidence:** ECOWAS members disagreed about intervention, and later diplomacy became more prominent than force.
- **Caution:** The web page itself is only the landing page; the operative content comes from the communique PDF and supporting reporting.
- **Independent support:** Reuters reporting on sanctions and force threat; DW reporting on the intervention debate. ([reuters.com via Investing](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/west-african-leaders-meet-over-niger-coup-junta-warns-against-intervention-3138325), [dw.com](https://amp.dw.com/en/niger-how-might-an-ecowas-military-intervention-unfold/a-66431072))

3. **Tinubu publicly preferred diplomacy before kinetic action**
- **Claim:** On August 10 and again on August 31, 2023, Tinubu said ECOWAS would prioritize diplomacy and dialogue and that all diplomatic options would be exhausted before force. This matters because it is the most direct evidence of his justification standard: he did not publicly jump straight to war, but instead framed force as a last resort.
- **Best source:** State House, “Niger Republic: At 2nd ECOWAS Extraordinary Summit, President Tinubu Champions Dialogue to Resolve Impasse,” August 10, 2023; and “President Tinubu to NSCIA: Nobody is Interested in War but Sanctions Relief can only Result from Niger Junta’s Positive Change in Posture,” August 31, 2023. Direct links: [statehouse.gov.ng](https://statehouse.gov.ng/niger-republic-at-2nd-ecowas-extraordinary-summit-president-tinubu-champions-dialogue-to-resolve-impasse/), [statehouse.gov.ng](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-to-nscia-nobody-is-interested-in-war-but-sanctions-relief-can-only-result-from-niger-juntas-positive-change-in-posture/)
- **Locator:** The August 10 release says diplomacy and dialogue are the “bedrock” of the approach and that all avenues should be exhausted. The August 31 statement says “all diplomatic options will be exhausted” before military intervention. ([statehouse.gov.ng](https://statehouse.gov.ng/niger-republic-at-2nd-ecowas-extraordinary-summit-president-tinubu-champions-dialogue-to-resolve-impasse/), [statehouse.gov.ng](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-to-nscia-nobody-is-interested-in-war-but-sanctions-relief-can-only-result-from-niger-juntas-positive-change-in-posture/))
- **Period type:** Target-period contemporaneous.
- **Ruler attribution:** Direct.
- **Complicating evidence:** He also said the kinetic option had not been abandoned, so this was restraint, not pacifism.
- **Caution:** Official statements are self-justifying and do not prove implementation quality.
- **Independent support:** Reuters and Semafor both reported the same diplomatic emphasis. ([semafor.com](https://www.semafor.com/article/08/10/2023/niger-coup-diplomatic-negotiations), [theprint.in](https://theprint.in/world/west-africas-ecowas-rejects-niger-juntas-proposed-three-year-delay-for-elections/1725046/))

4. **Domestic and regional checks pushed Tinubu toward restraint**
- **Claim:** Nigerian political actors and regional realities constrained Tinubu’s room for escalation. The Senate urged diplomatic options over military intervention, and DW’s reporting noted that Nigeria’s military was already tied down at home across many states. This matters because it shows that Tinubu was not free to treat Niger as an easy coercive expedition.
- **Best source:** DW, “Nigeria Senate cautions against Niger military intervention,” August 6, 2023; DW, “How might an ECOWAS military intervention unfold?,” August 5, 2023. Direct links: [dw.com](https://amp.dw.com/en/nigeria-senate-cautions-against-niger-military-intervention/a-66450388), [dw.com](https://amp.dw.com/en/niger-how-might-an-ecowas-military-intervention-unfold/a-66431072)
- **Locator:** DW says the Senate urged Tinubu to look into other options than force, and the intervention analysis says Nigeria’s army was “bogged down at home” and operating in many states. ([dw.com](https://amp.dw.com/en/nigeria-senate-cautions-against-niger-military-intervention/a-66450388), [dw.com](https://amp.dw.com/en/niger-how-might-an-ecowas-military-intervention-unfold/a-66431072))
- **Period type:** Target-period contemporaneous.
- **Ruler attribution:** Moderate. These are constraints on Tinubu, not commands by him.
- **Complicating evidence:** ECOWAS still kept the force option open, so restraint was strategic, not automatic.
- **Caution:** DW is secondary reporting and mixes analyst judgment with fact.
- **Independent support:** Guardian reporting on civil and religious leaders also urged diplomacy and warned against war. ([guardian.ng](https://guardian.ng/news/stakeholders-to-tinubu-sending-troops-to-niger-akin-to-leaving-leprosy-to-treat-ringworms/), [guardian.ng](https://guardian.ng/news/tinubu-sends-delegation-of-islamic-leaders-to-niger-republic-for-another-round-of-dialogue/))

**Information Environment and Evidence Limits**

- The record is unusually clearer on the diplomatic track than on any actual military plan, because there was no Nigerian war to observe and no troop deployment to evaluate.
- Official ECOWAS and State House sources are strong for dated positions and formal posture, but weak on independent assessment.
- Reuters-grade reporting and DW fill the gap on internal constraint, threat credibility, and the absence of easy military options.
- The main unresolved question is not whether Tinubu used force in 2023. He did not. The question is whether his coercive diplomacy improved regional stability or only prolonged a crisis while avoiding escalation.

**Concise Research Questions**

- Did ECOWAS sanctions under Tinubu materially improve the prospects for constitutional restoration, or mainly deepen humanitarian harm?
- How much of Tinubu’s restraint was principled diplomacy versus inability to mobilize a viable intervention?
- Did Nigeria’s Senate and other domestic actors exert real veto power, or only advisory pressure?
- What role did third-party mediators, especially religious leaders and former heads of state, play in preventing escalation?
- Did the Niger crisis leave a durable regional legal or institutional settlement, or only a temporary pause?

**Corroborating Sources Opened But Not Fully Extracted**

- [Congressional Research Service, *Nigeria: Overview and U.S. Policy*](https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/R47052)
- [House of Commons Library, *Nigeria: 2023 presidential election*](https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cbp-9738/)
- [Reuters summary via Investing, July 29, 2023](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/west-african-leaders-meet-over-niger-coup-junta-warns-against-intervention-3138325)
- [Reuters summary via ThePrint, August 13, 2023](https://theprint.in/world/west-africa-bloc-seeks-ways-to-engage-with-niger-junta/1713156/)
- [Reuters summary via ThePrint, August 16, 2023](https://theprint.in/world/niger-junta-says-open-to-talks-as-putin-us-stress-peace/1716140/)
- [Reuters summary via ThePrint, August 22, 2023](https://theprint.in/world/west-africas-ecowas-rejects-niger-juntas-proposed-three-year-delay-for-elections/1725046/)
- [The Guardian Nigeria, August 24-25, 2023 dialogue coverage](https://guardian.ng/news/tinubu-sends-delegation-of-islamic-leaders-to-niger-republic-for-another-round-of-dialogue/), [https://guardian.ng/news/coup-again-tinubu-sends-islamic-leaders-to-niger-for-dialogue/](https://guardian.ng/news/coup-again-tinubu-sends-islamic-leaders-to-niger-for-dialogue/)
- [The Guardian Nigeria, August 11, 2023 mediation analysis](https://guardian.ng/features/niger-coup-and-mediation-by-ulamau/)

**Promising Leads Still Needing Inspection**

- The actual ECOWAS communique PDF, to capture the precise sanctions, force, and dialogue language.
- Any Nigerian cabinet or parliamentary record showing whether Tinubu formally authorized or rejected a military proposal.
- Any official ECOWAS or Nigerian documentation on mediation missions to Niamey.
- Any casualty, displacement, or humanitarian-data source on the effects of sanctions and border closures.
- Any later 2024-2025 regional settlement record, if the question shifts from 2023 conduct to durable outcome.

**Labelled Source Groups**

- **Accepted evidence sources**
  - ECOWAS summit notice, July 28, 2023
  - ECOWAS final communique landing page, August 10, 2023
  - State House dialogue statements, August 10 and 31, 2023
  - DW Senate and intervention analysis, August 5-6, 2023

- **Corroboration sources**
  - Reuters reporting on sanctions and intervention threat
  - Reuters reporting on diplomatic search and later rejection of the junta’s timeline
  - Guardian reporting on Nigerian civil-society and clerical mediation
  - CRS and House of Commons context pieces

- **Unused but promising leads**
  - ECOWAS communique PDF
  - UN Security Council Niger statement
  - any formal Senate resolution text
  - any mediation mission reports

**Source Counts**

- Candidate sources inspected: 12+
- Evidence records retained: 4
- Corroboration sources opened: 8
- Major gaps remaining: 5
